page.title: Downloads
page.description: Download the sanitised Webconsulting TYPO3 Lab snapshot: database, Fileadmin archive and the install script.

content.bodytext:
A complete, self-contained copy of this lab: the database, the matching Fileadmin archive, and a script that wires both into a running DDEV site for you.

Downloads

  • install.txt — scripted setup, run with bash install.txt (3 KB)
  • db-public.zip — database, sanitised (10 MB)
  • fileadmin-public.zip — matching Fileadmin contents (352 MB)
  • snapshot-readme.txt — what is in the snapshot

Quick start

Requires Docker or OrbStack, DDEV 1.25.3 or newer, and Git. The downloads need the same credentials you used to reach this page.

curl -fLO https://typo3-lab.webconsulting.at/fileadmin/_downloads/install.txt
bash install.txt

It clones the repository, fetches both archives, and runs the documented bootstrap. Sign in at /typo3/ with admin / Demo123* and change that password.

The .txt and .zip extensions are deliberate. TYPO3 denies .sh and .sql files from the document root, and that rule is worth leaving intact. Zip rather than .tar.gz because Apache serves any .gz with Content-Encoding: gzip, which browsers silently decode — you would save a file named .tar.gz that is really a plain tar, and the import would reject it.

What “sanitised” means

The published database is not the one this site runs on. Twenty credential-bearing tables keep their structure but ship with no rows: Vault secrets, API and MCP access tokens, OAuth records, WorkOS identities, the LLM provider credential, every backend and frontend account, and the log and history tables. A single demo administrator is added in their place.

Integrations that need credentials therefore start switched off. Supply your own through the Vault backend module.

Import the database and the Fileadmin archive together — the database references files by uid, so a mismatched pair renders with broken images.
